items.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: she was a blind pianist... she loaned me that... I said, 'please loan me that' and she loaned it to me.

ctx.x: Bonnier? Probably B-O-N-N-I-E-R or something like that. Bess, well her name ended up being Bess Makras, M-A-K-R-A-S, um, she was a blind pianist. She had this little – she had this little box, a record player, that you could just take the thing and go like that and it could be in every key, all the back until you get to the other key, low. So she loaned me that, I said, “please loan me that” and she loaned it to me. I went home, I set it up and took a record and started learning how to solo. Now I don’t remember…
The sights, the sounds, the smells, when you were growing up. What were some of the things that you remember.
